title: Credentialing of Applicants and Re-application after Termination — Network Participation Agreements
content:
**Rule.** An application for one of the **Network Participation Agreements** is accepted only if four things hold:

- the applicant's specialty is one the agreement type admits;
- the location type is one the agreement type admits;
- the applicant has an active state license and a valid NPI;
- the applicant's professional liability limits are at least the agreement type's per-occurrence minimum and annual aggregate minimum.

A provider whose agreement ended for cause or by license action may apply again only after the for-cause re-application wait has run from the termination date of that earlier agreement.

## Committee decision

- The credentialing committee decides within the agreement type's turnaround days of the complete application.
- It decides on primary-source verifications no older than the agreement type's verification age limit.
- Agreements that require a site visit are approved only after the office passes it.
- An application that does not meet the requirements is denied.
- No application fee is charged (the application fee is 0.00 USD).

## On approval

- The agreement takes effect on the first day of the month after the decision.
- The recredentialing due date is the decision date plus the agreement type's recredentialing cycle in months.
- The fee schedule for the agreement type and service state is assigned.
- Services rendered before the effective date are out of network.

## Re-application wait

| Element | Basis |
|---|---|
| Records consulted | Cascade's record of the earlier agreement for the same NPI: its termination date and termination reason. This is a system record, read before the application is accepted. |
| Clock starts | The termination date of that earlier agreement |
| Length after a for-cause or license-action termination | The agreement type's for-cause re-application wait, in calendar months |
| Length after a termination without cause | The shorter without-cause re-application wait, counted the same way |
| Counting | Calendar months from the termination date. Where the target day does not exist in the resulting month, the last day of that month is used. |
| Comparison | An application on or after the resulting date is accepted; the resulting date itself is included |

### Boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

- A DHMO specialist agreement, whose for-cause wait is 24 months, ended for cause on 31 August of a given year. The wait ends on 31 August two years later. An application received that day is accepted. One received on 30 August of that year is not.
- A savings network agreement, whose for-cause wait is 12 months, ended by license action on 29 February of a leap year. The following year has no 29 February, so the resulting date is 28 February. An application on 28 February is accepted; one on 27 February is not.
- A savings network agreement ended without cause. Its without-cause wait is 0 months, so the resulting date is the termination date itself, and an application on or after that date is accepted.

## Effective date example (hypothetical)

The committee approves a provider on 14 June. The agreement takes effect on 1 July. A cleaning performed on 20 June is out of network.
